title: Streamline model onboarding and release verification with signed artifacts and profile publishing
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement an end-to-end CI/CD flow that builds model artifacts, produces/verifies cryptographic provenance, generates performance profiles from the bench runner, and promotes signed artifacts to the model catalog with version pinning and automated canary release gates. The flow should be resilient, auditable, and support constrained rollout policies for Dedicated and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A GitHub Actions workflow (or equivalent) builds model artifacts reproducibly and stores outputs in the artifact bucket with a deterministic path
Every artifact has a signed provenance bundle (cosign/sigstore or equivalent) and a SLSA-compatible attestation linked to the artifact ID
Performance profile generation job runs automatically against the common bench suite and uploads a profile JSON to /profiles/{model}/{version}/{profile-id}.json
The model registry entry is created/updated with pinned version metadata and references to signed artifacts + profile IDs
Promotion stage enforces automated checks: signature verified, perf profile within allowed regression threshold, security review flag present if required
Automated canary rollout to dedicated pool (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with SLO/quality gates; rollback policy triggers on >5% error rate or latency SLO breach
Audit log entries exist for build, sign, publish, and promotion actions and are queryable from Console
Docs and runbook updated: onboarding checklist, troubleshooting steps, and how to revoke/promote artifacts
design_notes: Use cosign for signing model artifacts and attach a SLSA provenance statement to support attestation and future compliance requirements
Produce performance profiles via the bench runner in an isolated test cluster using pinned runtime and kernel variants to ensure stable profiles
Store artifacts & profiles in the existing model-catalog bucket with immutable paths and lifecycle rules; leverage object versioning for rollbacks
Introduce a small metadata layer (flat JSON) in the registry documenting: artifact URI, signature URI, profile URI, runtime-constraints, and pinned boolean
Promotion flow should be split into: build -> sign -> profile -> verify -> publish -> rollout. Each step emits events to the Console and audit logs
Avoid embedding secrets in the runner; use short-lived Workload Identity credentials and KMS-wrapped signing keys (HSM-backed where required)
implementation_plan: 1) Add GH Actions job `build-model-artifact` to compile, package, and upload artifacts to s3://model-catalog/dev/{model}/{sha}/
2) Integrate cosign signing step that produces a signature blob and a provenance attestation uploaded next to the artifact
3) Add `bench-runner` job that consumes the built artifact, runs standard perf suites, and writes a profile JSON to s3://model-catalog/profiles/{model}/{version}/{profile-id}.json
4) Implement registry webhook that verifies signature + profile and creates a pinned version entry in the model registry (service endpoint: /api/registry/pin)
5) Implement promotion workflow in infra: canary rollout controller that accepts release policy and schedules traffic weights, with hooks to monitor SLOs
6) Wire Console observability: show artifact signature status, profile diffs, and promotion progress with rollback button
7) Add automated tests for reproducible build, signature verification, and profile generation in CI to prevent regressions
8) Create runbook and a short demo script for Solutions and Sales engineers
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives from performance noise could block promotions. Mitigation: use repeated profiling and median values; require at least 3 runs and a statistical tolerance window
Risk: Signing keys compromise. Mitigation: rotate keys regularly, use HSM/KMS, require 2-person approval for production key changes
Risk: Large profile upload costs and storage. Mitigation: compress profiles, TTL for intermediate profiles, and keep canonical profiles only
Risk: Backwards compatibility for older runtime variants. Mitigation: record runtime constraints in profile metadata and allow fallback model variants in routing
